The tire demounting device comprises a hook member designed to engage and remove a tire from the edge of a wheel rim. The hook member includes an elongate body having a hook-shaped portion at one end and a connection point at the opposite end. The hook-shaped portion is configured to be inserted between the tire bead and the edge of the rim, while the connection point allows the hook member to be coupled to the mechanism that controls its movement.

The hook member is arranged between a pair of substantially parallel plates. These plates define a guide and support structure within which the hook member can move. In particular, the hook member is capable of performing a combined rotary and translational movement, or roto-translational movement, between the plates. This allows the hook to be accurately positioned relative to the tire and rim during both insertion and removal operations.

The pair of parallel plates is connected to a support element by means of a connection system. The support element may form part of a larger tire-changing machine or may be associated with a movable arm or frame of such a machine. The connection system provides a stable mechanical link between the plates and the support element, while allowing the demounting device to be positioned correctly with respect to the wheel.

A drive system is provided to move the body of the hook member between at least two operating positions. In a first, inserted position, the hook-shaped end of the hook member is introduced between the tire and the edge of the rim so that it can engage the tire bead. In a second, removal position, the hook member is moved in such a way as to lift or draw the tire bead away from the rim, thereby enabling removal of the tire from the wheel.

The movement of the hook body is controlled by a connecting rod and guided pin arrangement. The connecting rod is operatively connected to the hook body, while one or more pins associated with the hook body are guided along a shaped guide track formed in the parallel plates. As the drive system actuates the mechanism, the interaction between the connecting rod, the guided pin, and the shaped guide track causes the hook body to rotate and translate in a predetermined manner. This guided roto-translational motion ensures that the hook follows an optimized path, allowing reliable insertion between the tire and rim and effective removal of the tire while reducing the risk of damage to the rim or tire.
outputs.L4:
A tire demounting device is provided for removing a tire from a wheel rim in a controlled and reliable manner. The device includes a support structure on which a hook member is mounted, the hook member being arranged to engage a bead of the tire and lift or draw it away from the rim during a demounting operation.

The hook member is positioned between two substantially parallel guide plates. These plates define and constrain the path of movement of the hook, ensuring that the hook follows a predetermined trajectory rather than moving freely or unpredictably. In use, the hook is first brought into an insertion position, in which it can be introduced between the tire bead and the edge of the rim. From this position, the hook is moved through a guided path toward a removal position, in which the tire bead is displaced sufficiently to allow the tire to be separated from the rim.

Movement of the hook member is produced by a connection and drive system. This system includes a connecting rod operatively linked to the hook member and driven by a suitable actuator or drive mechanism. A pin associated with the connecting rod engages shaped guide tracks formed in or associated with the parallel plates. As the drive system operates, the pin travels along these shaped tracks, causing the connecting rod and hook member to move according to a controlled pattern.

The shaped tracks are configured to generate a combined rotational and translational movement of the hook member. In other words, the hook does not merely slide in a straight line, nor does it simply pivot about a fixed point. Instead, it performs a roto-translational motion that allows it to enter the space between the tire and rim, securely engage the tire bead, and then withdraw or lift the bead in a manner suited to the geometry of the wheel. This guided motion improves the precision and effectiveness of the demounting process.

By controlling the path of the hook through the cooperation of the pin, connecting rod, and shaped guide tracks, the device reduces the risk of improper engagement with the tire or rim. The parallel guide plates provide stability and maintain alignment of the hook during operation, while the drive system supplies the force necessary to move the hook from the insertion position to the removal position. As a result, the device enables efficient tire removal while helping to avoid damage to the tire bead, the rim edge, or other wheel components.

The demounting device is therefore particularly useful in tire-changing machines or similar equipment where repeatable, accurate, and force-controlled movement is required. The combination of a guided hook member, shaped tracks, and a connecting rod drive arrangement provides a compact and mechanically reliable solution for separating a tire from a rim with improved control and precision.

## A Tire Demounting: What It Is and Why It Matters

A tire demounting is the process of removing a tire from a wheel rim. This is commonly done when a tire is damaged, worn out, needs repair, or must be replaced with a seasonal tire. Proper tire demounting is important because it helps protect both the tire and the wheel from unnecessary damage.

The process usually requires specialized equipment, such as a tire changer, bead breaker, and mounting tools. First, the air is released from the tire. Then, the bead of the tire is separated from the rim. Once the bead is loosened, the tire can be carefully lifted off the wheel using the machine or appropriate hand tools.

A tire demounting should be performed with care, especially on modern wheels that may have tire pressure monitoring sensors, alloy rims, or low-profile tires. Incorrect handling can scratch the rim, damage the bead, or break a sensor. For this reason, many vehicle owners choose to have tire demounting done by trained technicians.

Whether for tire repair, replacement, recycling, or seasonal changeover, tire demounting is a necessary part of vehicle maintenance. Using the right equipment and technique ensures a safe, efficient, and damage-free tire service.
